candidate_analysis.explanation: The Random Forest classifies this binary as malware with probability 0.9950. All 20 top SHAP n-grams push toward cryptojacking, and none pushes the other way. Several of them are consistent with compute-heavy cryptographic or hashing code. Rotate instructions appear in ADD ROR (+0.008367), MOV ROL (+0.007454) and MOVZX ROL (+0.005150). These are typical of hash-function mixing rounds. BSWAP LEA (+0.005892) suggests endianness conversion, which is common when handling hash state or digests. The carry/borrow arithmetic chains SUB SBB (+0.009049), SBB INC (+0.006367), ADC SUB (+0.005855), SUB ADC (+0.005638) and XOR ADC (+0.004947) point to multi-word arithmetic or tightly interleaved mixing. SHL XCHG (+0.005099) and POP XCHG (+0.005249) add further register-shuffling and bit-manipulation behavior. The stack and call-convention n-grams DEC PUSH, ADD PUSH, POP CALL, POP PUSH, POP LEA, POP SUB, MOVZX PUSH, PUSH CALL (frequency 0.021853) and CALL PUSH (frequency 0.018470) are generic compiler-style code. They still carry positive SHAP weight, so the model treats the overall instruction mix as characteristic of the malware class. Each individual contribution is modest (about 0.005 to 0.009), so the verdict rests on the accumulation of many consistent signals rather than any single decisive pattern. The evidence contains no function-level attribution, API references or string data, so the crypto-like interpretation is an inference from mnemonic patterns only. Rotation, byte-swap and carry-chain n-grams also occur in legitimate crypto, compression and packing code. Even so, the model probability and the uniform direction of all 20 features support a high-confidence tier.

Call followed by a push, a generic control-flow pattern. Its high frequency (0.018470) suggests many small call-based routines. It contributes modestly.
